1.text:
The new chapter begins with three letters and no sentence. "Alif-Lãm-Mĩm" is written in the chapter as it is recited, and the sources discuss what an opening of that kind does, since a hearer is given letters he already knows and no statement built out of them, which is why one source reads the letters as a demonstration of an inability, the Arabs being asked to bring a chapter like this book and unable to do it while the material of the book is their own speech. Another reads them as a summons to attend, a way of stopping a listener at the door of what follows, and an account preserves a reciter telling his people that God informed him about the story of a delegation while these letters were being recited, so the letters carry a weight the audience could feel rather than a puzzle to be solved. Nothing in the verse explains them, and the sources do not agree on a single meaning for them, which is the shape of the verse's instruction, since a chapter that opens without a proposition asks a reader to wait for what the chapter will say, and the verses after this take up a book, a witness and a chain of prophets. The chapter's own opening is also the place where the question of who could bring such a speech is settled, and the answer given there is that an entire community was held back from it, so the letters carry the claim of the book that follows without arguing for it.

**Alif-Lãm-Mĩm, the inability of a people to bring a book like this one, and the story a reciter was told.**

It is said that by listening to these disconnected letters [Alif Lām Mīm] which are contrary to the ordinary customs of human discourse every concept disappears from the hearts whether it be a known written cus tomary or imagined thing and whether it arises from necessity Ḍarūra sensory perception ḥiss or independent reasoning ijtihād. They indicate the inability of the Arabs to bring a Qur’ān like this one despite the fact that it is composed of letters similar to the ones at the beginning of this Sūrah, which also form the parts of their own speech. (Alif. Lam. Mim.) that he said: 'Allah informed us about the story of the delegation of Najran; it is also said that this is an oath by which Allah swore that He is One and that He has neither progeny nor partner. (In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)(1. Alif-Lam-Mim.)(2. Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists.)(3. It is He Who has sent down the Book to you with truth, confirming what came before it. And He sent down the Tawrah and the Injil,)(4. Aforetime, as a guidance to mankind. And He sent down the criterion. Truly, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah, for them there is a severe torment; and Allah is All-Mighty, All-Able of Retribution.)

**The chain of prophets, the agreement of a large number of people, and an age when writing was not in vogue.**

This is the golden chain of prophets from Sayyidna Adam to the Last of the Prophets upto whose time some one hundred and twenty four thousand blessed prophets were born in different periods, speaking different languages, living in different countries. The agreement of a large number of people on a certain principle from the very beginning of humanity may be taken as a natural proof of its reality, if they belong to different times and places, having no means of communicating with each other. They were in an age when, communication through writing was not in vogue, which could make it possible for one prophet to have access to the books and writings of another and might help him to pick up the call of the earlier prophets as his own. The consensus of such a large group of persons consisting of not less than one hundred and twenty four thousand men of different times and places may be enough for establishing the principle, even regardless of their intrinsic trustworthiness. After that, by be-ginning the Surah Al-Baqarah with 1 ‌ (This Book which has no doubt in it), it was pointed out that the prayer made in Su-rah Al-Fatihah for guidance to the straight path has been accepted and Allah Almighty has sent down this Qur'an which provides guidance to the straight path.

**Hearts emptied of what they have imagined, the prayer made so that a people could prevail, and the invitation to look at a power and a wisdom.**

When the hearts are emptied of imagined and known concepts and the innermost selves are purified of customary and familiar things the name Allāh comes to a heart sanctified from everything other [than Him] and to an innermost self purified of every mode [of inquiry] kayf. Since the prayer was made in order that Muslims could confront and prevail over the disbelievers, it was in consonance with that prayer that, in the following Surah 'Al- Imran, the text deals with the modalities of dealing with disbelievers, as well as, with the need to carry out Jihad against them, verbally and physically. Lastly, while referring to the absolute power and wisdom of Allah Almighty, verse 6 invites one's attention to the fact that Allah shapes all men and women in the wombs of their mothers according to His supreme wisdom which has created billions of men and women with clear distinguishable features establishing the identity of each individual distinct from all others.

2.text:
The letters are followed at once by a statement, and the sentence is a testimony before it is a description. "Allah! There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining" names the one who is not shared with, then gives two of his qualities, and the sources observe that the order puts the denial and the exception first so that a reader arrives at the attributes through a refusal rather than through an argument. The wording of the first half is about what a person may turn to, and the phrase there is no god is handled as a denial of any other claim on a worshipper rather than a claim about a being who is merely stronger, while the two names that follow are read as the ground on which that refusal stands, a life that has no end and a sustaining of what exists. One source takes the verse as a rational proof of an oneness, on the ground that a thing which cannot bring itself into being and cannot keep itself in being cannot be the one a person bows to, and that the highest point of independence belongs only to what needs nothing. What is brought to the letters beside this treats the whole opening as a claim about speech rather than about a doctrine, so the chapter begins with a testimony and a proof laid side by side, and the verse after this takes up the book in which both are stated.

**The first word at the head of the chapter, and the set of letters a statement is made beside.**

The first word, Alif Lam Mim at the head of the first verse be-longs to the special set of words used by the Qur'an which are words of hidden meaning and are known as Mutashabihat the real meaning of which is a secret between Allah and His Messenger and the details of which appear a little later in the section. In the words (Allah: there is no god but He) which follow immediately, the doctrine of the Oneness of Allah has been put forth as a categorical declaration. Surah Āl-'Imrān was revealed in Al-Madīnah, as evident by the fact that the first eighty-three Ayat in it relate to the delegation from Najran that arrived in Al-Madīnah on the ninth year of Hijrah (632 CE).

**A rational proof of an oneness, and the highest point a thing being worshipped must occupy.**

The first verse of this section presents a rational proof of the Oneness of Allah; the second verse, the reported proof 1, followed by an answer to some doubts nursed by disbelievers towards the later part. In the terminology of Islamic theology, a proof based on rational argument is called rational proof while a proof based on a verse of divine book or on a declaration made by an authority or a report narrated by a trustworthy person is called a reported proof. It, therefore, requires that the one who is being worshipped must occupy the highest point of honour and power and who has to be most perfect from all angles.

**What has no power to come into being, a being that is dependent for its own being, and the bowing a truth asks for.**

Therefore, it is crystal clear that all things in this world which have no power to come into being by themselves, nor can they sustain it - be they idols carved in stone, or water, or trees, or angels and apostles - none of them is worthy of worship. From this it is obvious that anything which cannot sustain its own being, rather is dependent upon somebody else for its very existence, could hardly claim to have any honour or power in its own right. Bowing to the truth required them to bow to the Prophet and to God, and they thought that by surrendering to the Supreme Being and His Prophet they would diminish in stature.

**The One who lives without death or deficiency, the Self-subsistent Creator of the world, and the creation that exists through Him.**

He is the One Who lives perfectly without any death or deficiency. (Allah! There is no God save Him, the Alive) Who dies not and is not evanescent, (the Eternal) the Self-subsistent Who has no beginning. He exists by Himself and is not in need of any of His creation. The creation only exists through Him and is always in need of Him.

3.text:
The chapter moves from a testimony about who God is to a statement about what was sent, and the address is the reason the two belong together. "He has revealed to you O Prophet the Book in truth" gives the book a manner as well as an origin, and the wording of the manner is about truth rather than about beauty or persuasiveness, so the sources read the clause as an answer to a doubt about where the book came from, with the phrase in truth standing against the claim that a man composed it. "confirming what came before it" then places this book among earlier books rather than against them, and the wording is careful, since a confirmation is not a repetition, and the sources discuss what a later book confirms in an earlier one, which is the same question the next clause raises. "as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel" names two of those books and puts them in the same sentence with the same verb, so the Torah and the Gospel are described as things sent down in the manner the verse has just used for this book, with the remark that whenever the Qur'an speaks of the two it means the books themselves rather than the copies a community now has. A reader is left with a chain, a book that testifies to what came before it and a God whose speech is one in its truth, and the verse after this tells what was done with those earlier books and what follows for the people who turn from them. The order within the verse is worth noticing, since the Book of this prophet is named first and the two earlier books are named after it with a repeated verb, and the address that opens the clause is not carried over into that second half, so the Torah and the Gospel are spoken of as things sent to prophets before him rather than as a possession of his own community; a confirmation is therefore given as a relation between two revelations and not as an appeal to their authority, which is how the sources take the phrase in truth, as the quality the later book brings to the earlier ones and not the quality it borrows from them.

**The Book revealed with truth, and the prophet who was told what he had not known.**

(He hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture) He sent you Gabriel with the Scripture (with truth) in order to show truth from falsehood, (confirming) corroborating Allah's divine Oneness (that which was (revealed) before it) of scriptures, (even as He revealed the Torah) in one go to Moses the son of Amran (and the Gospel) in one go to the Jesus the son of Mary. (It is He Who has sent down the Book to you with truth,) means, revealed the Qur'an to you, O Muhammad, in truth, meaning there is no doubt or suspicion that it is revealed from Allah. He has revealed to you, O Prophet, the Qur’ān with true stories and just laws that are in agreement with the previous divine books; and there is no contradiction between all these divine books. He has revealed to you the Book by the truth You did not know O Muḥammad what the Book was nor the story of the lovers.

**The Torah and the Gospel sent down before, and the books that testify to the truth of this one.**

Whenever the Holy Qur'an speaks of the 'Torah and the Injil' it refers to the original books revealed to the prophets Moses and Jesus . (Confirming what came before it) means, from the previous divinely revealed Books, sent to the servants and Prophets of Allah. These Books testify to the truth of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an also testifies to the truth these Books contained, including the news and glad tidings of Muhammad's prophethood and the revelation of the Glorious Qur'an. (And He sent down the Tawrah) to Musa (Musa) son of 'Imran,. That is to say Even though We revealed Our books to the messengers before you We did not omit the remembrance dhikr of you from any book.

**A principle that is not a mere philosophy, the Book sent down to a man who did not know it, and the virtues mentioned with this chapter.**

Briefly stated, it means that the principle of tauhid as de-scribed in the Holy Qur'an is not something peculiar to the Qur'an or the Prophet of Islam. We should also state that we mentioned the virtues of Surah Āl-'Imrān along with the virtues of Surat Al-Baqarah in the beginning of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Baqarah. On the contrary, Allah Almighty has sent Scrip-tures such as the Torah and the Injil, and His prophets, in earlier times.

4.text:
The verse carries the earlier books into the past tense and then turns on the people who refused them. "previously, as a guide for people" attaches to what was revealed before this book, and the wording is about guidance given to people rather than to one community, which is why the sources read the clause as a claim about the reach of the earlier scriptures and not only about their age. "and also revealed the Standard to distinguish between right and wrong" names the fourth thing in the verse, and the wording of a standard is handled by the sources as a cut rather than a hint, a thing that separates a true matter from a false one, so a book that guides is joined to a criterion that decides. "Surely those who reject Allah's revelations will suffer a severe torment" then gives the consequence of refusal, and this with the remark that the verse does not promise a punishment proportionate to the crime but a severe one, which is read against the fact that these people were given a criterion and did not use it. "For Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment" ends the verse on two qualities, a might and an ability to requite, and the sources treat the second as the reason the torment is certain rather than merely possible, since a criterion that decides nothing for anyone would be of no use to a book at all. A reader of the passage so far has been given a book, a confirmation, a Torah, a Gospel, a standard and now a reckoning, and the next verse removes the last place a person can hide, which is the reason the two verses are usually read as one movement rather than as two separate statements about knowledge and about power. Four things are named in this verse and its first half, a Book, a confirmation, a guidance and a Criterion, and the sources keep the third and the fourth apart, since a guidance leads a person who is willing to be led and a Criterion decides a case whether or not anyone attends to it, which is the ground on which the threat that follows is read as the closing of an argument rather than as an outburst, a people having been given the means to tell one matter from another and having declined to use them.

**A guidance for people aforetime, and the Criterion sent down to distinguish a true matter from a false one.**

before that is to say before revealing it the Qur’ān as guidance hudan a circumstantial qualifier meaning hādiyīn ‘guides from error’ to people to those who followed these two Books He uses the word anzala for the revelation of these two and nazzala for that of the Qur’ān for the latter entails repetition whereas the two Books were revealed in one instance; and He revealed the Criterion al-furqān meaning the Scriptures that discriminate between truth and falsehood. (Aforetime) before Muhammad and the Qur'an, (for a guidance to mankind) as a guidance from error to the Children of Israel; (and hath revealed the Criterion (of right and wrong) He revealed the Qur'an to Muhammad in instalments to differentiate the lawful from the unlawful. (And He sent down the criterion) which is the distinction between misguidance, falsehood and deviation on one hand, and guidance, truth and piety on the other hand. He revealed the Criterion to differentiate between truth and falsehood, and between guidance and misguidance. The Quran is not only a genuine book of guidance but also serves as the criterion or standard of right and wrong. Whenever the Holy Qur'an speaks of the 'Torah and the Injil' it refers to the original books revealed to the prophets Moses and Jesus . (Confirming what came before it) means, from the previous divinely revealed Books, sent to the servants and Prophets of Allah.

**Those who reject the signs, the terrible chastisement that awaits them, and the eyes and minds that were granted and refused.**

As for those who disbelieve in God’s signs the Qur’ān or any other revelation for them awaits a terrible chastisement; God is Mighty victorious in His affair so that nothing can prevent Him from effecting His promise and His threat; Lord of Retribution with a severe punishment for those that disobeyed Him the like of which none can do. As for those who disbelieve in God's signs for them awaits a terrible chastisement. [The chastisement] is the ignominy of the veil but they do not perceive [this]. (Lo! those who disbelieve the revelations of Allah) Muhammad and the Qur'an, referring in this context to the delegation of Najran, (theirs will be a heavy doom) in this world and in the next. These are the people to whom their Creator granted minds, but who failed to understand the truth when it came to them in the form of arguments. These are the people to whom God granted eyes, but who failed to see the light (sent by God in the form of this book). (Truly, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah) means they denied, refused and unjustly rejected them,. Now those who, denying the book of the Almighty, refuse to abandon the religion devised by human beings, are deserving of His punishment.

**Mighty and able to requite, the retribution taken from those who reject His messengers, and the sovereignty whose grandeur is invincible.**

(All-Able of Retribution.) from those who reject His Ayat and defy His honorable Messengers and great Prophets. (And Allah is All-Mighty) meaning, His grandeur is invincible and His sovereignty is infinite,. (Allah is Mighty) powerful in His vengeance, (Able to Requite (the wrong) able to carry His vengeance out on them. He is also able to take retribution from those who reject His messengers and go against His instruction. Anyone having imperfect knowledge and limited power can-not be entrusted with this exalted station.

**The guidance sent for man throughout the ages, the final book sent in accordance with a plan, and a religion devised by human beings.**

He has sent guidance for man throughout the ages, including the Torah and the Bible, which were revealed to the former prophets. Ultimately, in accordance with God’s plan, the final book in the form of the Quran was sent down to man. It tells us which is the true religion and which is the religion devised by human beings through misinterpretation. All of these divine books contained guidance and directed people to the best of this world and theAfterlife. On the contrary, Allah Almighty has sent Scrip-tures such as the Torah and the Injil, and His prophets, in earlier times.

**The matter of a pre-eternal choosing that came suddenly, and the books revealed to the messengers before.**

But a matter of pre-eternal choosing came suddenly upon you and cast you into an amazing affair its proof sublime its place of descent and occurrence precious. confirming what was before it that is verifying His promise to you in the books that came through the prophets [ ]. and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before as guidance to people and He revealed the criterion. That is to say Even though We revealed Our books to the messengers before you We did not omit the remembrance dhikr of you from any book. God is Precious ʿazīz to His friends Lord of Retribution to His enemies. It did not present any new claim which could pose problems for people in its understanding or acceptance. He mentions this Criterion after He has mentioned the three Scriptures so that it encompasses all revealed Scriptures besides these.

5.text:
The verse is one clause long and it closes the space the previous verses had been describing. "Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah" takes the two places a person can act in and removes from both of them anything hidden, so the criterion that was sent down to distinguish a true matter from a false one is joined now to a knowledge that has already reached every case, and a reader is left with a decision that is not only offered but watched. The sources read the clause as the ground of what came before it, since a book and a standard would be of no use to a people who could put them aside without being accounted with, and one of them takes the two verses of this opening as a fortification of the doctrine of an oneness, on the ground that the qualities named in them, a life without end, a sustaining of what exists and a knowledge that misses nothing, belong only to a being that needs nothing. Another source puts the point higher, with the statement that a course of action for a person can be determined only by a being who has known the whole of his nature and made it, which makes the verse the reason a law can be trusted rather than merely obeyed. A reader who has been told that a severe torment awaits those who refuse is given here the reason a refusal cannot be kept, and the next verse turns from what is hidden to what is made, in the wombs, PLACEHOLDER_NOT_USED

**The being who knows the whole nature of a person and determines the course he should take.**

It is, therefore, only God who, after placing the nature of man in the perspective of the entire universe, may decree what kind of conduct will guarantee man’s success in this world and the next, for a sound human mentality can only be one which is in harmony with the rest of the world and in complete accord with the vaster system of the cosmos. The right course of action for man can be determined only by a Being who has not only known man from his birth to his death, but also knows what has gone before his birth and what will happen after his death.

**No one presents a need except that it is satisfied, nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth, and the reader eager for the knowledge a book describes.**

As for the elect khuṣūṣ no one presents a need to Him except He satisfies it qāḌīhā and no one has any resource in a calamity except He suffices for it kāfīhā. And He has made this so clear in His Book, that any reader who is eager for knowledge of Him will certainly gain enlightenment from it. Briefly stated, it means that the principle of tauhid as de-scribed in the Holy Qur'an is not something peculiar to the Qur'an or the Prophet of Islam. Nothing no existent thing whatever is hidden in heaven and earth from God on account of His knowledge of universals and particulars. Allah states that He has perfect knowledge in the heavens and earth and that nothing in them is hidden from His watch.

**What is made so clear in the book, the trust a person places in his Maker, and the doctrine the qualities fortify.**

This being so, the only realistic approach for man is to trust in His Maker and accept and follow His guidance wholeheartedly and with full confidence. The last two verses further fortify the doctrine of tauhid on the ground that the attributes of encompassing knowledge and unlimited power are strong proofs of His being the One who possesses the eternal, and all-encompassing knowledge and whose power controls every-thing, and that He is the only One who rightly deserves to be wor-shipped. Truly, nothing is hidden from Allah, in the earth or in the heaven He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. Anyone having imperfect knowledge and limited power can-not be entrusted with this exalted station.
